A1.justification: Both PDFs describe PersistWorld and contain readable main texts, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–E. Corresponding content can be matched despite layout changes and added experiments.

before.justification: v1 reports original DROID rollout evaluations, ablations, a human preference study, and comparisons between simulated and real-robot policy performance.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds baseline comparisons, Bridge and RT-1 evaluations, and a real-robot policy-improvement experiment.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.4 and Algorithm 1 retain the same model, contrastive denoising objective, randomized prefix branching, multi-view rewards, and LoRA/action-encoder updates. The new regression and reward variants are comparison experiments, not revisions to the proposed algorithm.

E1.justification: v2 extends training and evaluation to Bridge with WidowX and RT-1 with Google Robot, beyond the retained DROID setting. It also adds policy improvement on a four-block spatial picking task, distinct from v1's three policy-evaluation tasks.

E2.justification: v2 adds two substantive controls: a Self-Forcing-style baseline trained on generated histories to regress ground-truth latents, and an HPSv3 reward replacement in Table 13. These are adapted comparisons, not full reproductions of Self-Forcing or WorldCompass. The original world-model baselines and WorldCompass curriculum comparison remain.

E3.justification: The reported main post-training budget changes from 8,000 to 6,000 steps; this does not establish that the retained results were rerun. New experimental designs include 100,000-step SVD adaptation on Bridge and RT-1, and full pi0 finetuning on 50 rollouts from each world model followed by five real-robot trials per block.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained Appendix B ablations, v2 tests whether RL adds value over training on generated histories and compares their learning curves in Figure 13. Table 13 adds an analysis of perceptual rewards versus HPSv3, covering both visual fidelity and training cost.

E5.justification: The paired-comparison significance, policy-correlation p-values, and Appendix D's inter-rater agreement, binomial test, and confidence interval are retained. The added experiments introduce no new uncertainty-estimation or multi-seed reporting practice.

E6.justification: Original DROID table values remain unchanged. Newly reported comparisons include Bridge PSNR of 25.20 versus 26.36 and RT-1 PSNR of 23.81 versus 26.63 for SVD versus PersistWorld, HPSv3 versus perceptual-reward results, and Self-Forcing-style scores and learning curves. The new policy experiment reports progression of 0.350 for the base policy, 0.558 with Ctrl-World, and 0.667 with PersistWorld. Section 4 also corrects the masked-wrist SSIM gain from 5.4% to 4.1%, consistent with unchanged Table 2.

T1.justification: The mathematical objective and Appendix A's definitions, assumptions, posterior-mixture lemma, optimal-predictor theorem, proofs, and parameterization argument are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's four contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about RL post-training, randomized branching, multi-view rewards, and DROID rollout quality. The additional experiments strengthen supporting evidence without substantively reformulating these core claims.

C2.justification: v2 explains why text-image HPSv3 rewards cannot directly assess action-conditioned trajectory consistency and why the unavailable teacher motivates an adapted Self-Forcing comparison. It also identifies rollout generation as the dominant training cost. Existing limitations concerning computation and absent explicit physical constraints remain.

D1.justification: Reported training time changes from three to two days on the same eight H200 GPUs. v2 documents settings for the added studies, including SVD adaptation steps, the HPSv3 task prompt, the top-k=2 reward comparison, and policy finetuning details. The core pseudocode, inference settings, and project access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to RT-1, Bridge, Self-Forcing, Rolling Forcing, and HPSv3. It extends the existing WorldCompass positioning through reward comparisons and discusses the applicability of forcing-based methods, while retaining most related-work discussion.

P1.justification: Changes comprise targeted additions to Section 4 and Appendix E.2, a main-text summary of the already existing Appendix C policy-evaluation results, and small language, author-formatting, and acknowledgement edits. The overall organization and most existing prose remain stable.

P2.justification: v2 substantially expands experimental displays with Tables 13–14 and Figures 12–14, covering reward comparisons, additional embodiments, learning curves, and the policy-improvement setup. Table 2 and Figure 6 are relocated, and the document uses larger page margins. Existing figures and table structures are otherwise retained.

improvement.justification: v2 addresses important validation gaps in v1: the Self-Forcing-style control tests RL's added value, Table 14 establishes benefits on two additional robot embodiments, and the new policy experiment supplies direct real-robot improvement evidence beyond policy ranking. Together these substantially strengthen generality and practical relevance. Adapted comparators, limited experimental detail, and only five trials per block without new uncertainty estimates constrain the conclusions, but do not outweigh the substantial gain in supporting evidence.
